channel-capacity.label: Flip probability p
channel-capacity.description: A remote workshop sends a binary machine-status symbol: zero or one. Each use independently flips either symbol with probability p. A designer also chooses the long-run probability q of sending one. Change the channel or the chosen input mix, then compare the information delivered by that mix with the channel’s best possible information per use.

channel-capacity.label: Chance of sending one q
channel-capacity.description: A remote workshop sends a binary machine-status symbol: zero or one. Each use independently flips either symbol with probability p. A designer also chooses the long-run probability q of sending one. Change the channel or the chosen input mix, then compare the information delivered by that mix with the channel’s best possible information per use.

channel-capacity.label: Channel capacity: a binary symmetric link primary result
channel-capacity.description: Channel capacity C is the largest mutual information per channel use among the allowed input distributions. For a memoryless binary symmetric channel with flip probability p, C=1−H₂(p) bits per use. A chosen probability q of sending one gives received-one chance t=p+q(1−2p) and mutual information I=H₂(t)−H₂(p). An equally likely input mix reaches the capacity; an uneven mix can supply less information through the same link.

channel-capacity.label: Current information for this input mix
channel-capacity.description: Follow the flip chance into noise entropy, calculate the received symbol mix, then subtract the noise entropy. The best input mix makes the output equally likely and reaches one minus the noise entropy.

hamming-code.label: Flipped position j · 0 means none
hamming-code.description: A workshop sends a four-bit machine-status label d through a wire as a seven-bit block c. Three added check bits overlap the data positions. Choose either a single flipped bit position j or no flip, then follow the received block r through its three parity checks into the repaired label u.

hamming-code.label: Four-bit data value d
hamming-code.description: A workshop sends a four-bit machine-status label d through a wire as a seven-bit block c. Three added check bits overlap the data positions. Choose either a single flipped bit position j or no flip, then follow the received block r through its three parity checks into the repaired label u.

hamming-code.label: Hamming code: locating one flipped bit primary result
hamming-code.description: A (7,4) Hamming code block adds three parity bits to four data bits. With even parity, the checks on positions 1,3,5,7; 2,3,6,7; and 4,5,6,7 produce bits s₁, s₂ and s₄. Their weighted sum s=s₁+2s₂+4s₄ is the syndrome. With no flip it is zero; with one flipped bit it gives that bit’s ordinary position from one through seven. This single-error correction step restores the encoded block and the original four-bit data.

hamming-code.label: Recovered four-bit label value
hamming-code.description: Encode four data bits with three even-parity checks, apply the chosen flip, and read the failed checks as a binary address. Repair that address and recover the original four-bit label.
